extracted.intended_audience: educators, educational theorists, policymakers, and students of education
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of criteria for aims and purposes of education within democratic societies, including what makes an educational aim 'good' and how social organization shapes educational ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education as a social process
rubrics_metrics.description: Since education is a social process, and there are many kinds of societies, a criterion for educational criticism and construction implies a particular social ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate educational forms by relating them to the kind of society they serve; the meaning of education is indeterminate until the social context/ideal is specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic criterion of education (two measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the worth of a form of social life by (1) the extent in which the interests of a group are shared by all its members, and (2) the fullness and freedom with which it interacts with other groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A democratic education promotes broadly shared interests and flexible, free intercourse with other groups; societies that set up barriers to communication and experience are undesirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education must secure equal participation and flexible institutional readjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: A society which makes provision for participation in its good of all its members on equal terms and which secures flexible readjustment of its institutions through interaction of the different forms of associated life is in so far democratic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether schools and education policy provide sufficient facilities and support to discount economic inequalities and retain youth under educational influence until they can master their economic/social careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education should promote supra‑national cooperation and de‑emphasize narrow nationalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis must be put upon whatever binds people together in cooperative human pursuits and results, apart from geographical limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate curricula and aims for whether they instill dispositions favoring broader human association over exclusive national sovereignty; avoid mere negative teaching (e.g., only 'teach the horrors of war').

rubrics_metrics.name: Education must give individuals personal interest and habits for orderly social change
rubrics_metrics.description: Such a society must have a type of education which gives individuals a personal interest in social relationships and control, and the habits of mind which secure social changes without introducing disorder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether education cultivates personal stake in collective affairs and the cognitive/emotional habits to enact social change while maintaining order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary aim: continued capacity for growth
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of education is to enable individuals to continue their education — the object and reward of learning is continued capacity for growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge programs by their ability to develop ongoing self‑directed learning capacity, not merely discrete learned facts or skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims must belong within the educative process (not be externally imposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are concerned with the contrast which exists when aims belong within the process in which they operate and when they are set up from without. An aim established externally to the process of action is always rigid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer aims that arise from the situation and activities of learners; externally supplied aims limit intelligence and reduce education to mechanical means‑end tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim requires intrinsic continuity and ordered activity
rubrics_metrics.description: An aim implies an orderly and ordered activity, one in which the order consists in the progressive completing of a process; the work assigned must possess intrinsic continuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid serial aggregates of disconnected acts (teacher‑dictated tasks lacking continuity) and also unstructured capricious action; good educational aims create cumulative, time‑extended activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim requires foresight, planning, and choice among alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: An aim means foresight in advance of the end; it gives direction to activity by (1) careful observation of conditions, (2) suggesting proper sequence of means, and (3) making choice of alternatives possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether aims encourage learners/teachers to observe conditions, sequence learning economically, and compare alternatives — acting with an aim is acting intelligently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting with an aim equals intelligent, purposeful activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Mind is capacity to refer present conditions to future results; acting with an aim is all one with acting intelligently and is a deliberate, observant, planning trait of activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess educational practices by whether they cultivate intentional, purposeful activity rather than passive reception or mere mechanical compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good aims must be outgrowths of existing conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim set up must be an outgrowth of existing conditions. It must be based upon a consideration of what is already going on; upon the resources and difficulties of the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject theoretical ends that are foreign to concrete situations; ensure aims take account of pupils' present experience, resources, and obstructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims must be tentative, experimental, and revisable
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim as it first emerges is a mere tentative sketch; acting upon it brings to light overlooked conditions, calling for revision. An aim must, then, be flexible; it must be capable of alteration to meet circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat aims as working hypotheses to be tested in action; prefer plans that are constantly revised in light of experience rather than rigid directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims must represent a freeing of activity (activity‑centred ends)
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim must always represent a freeing of activities — the doing with the thing, not possession of the thing; the object is a means of directing and continuing the activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor ends that specify kinds of active capacities (e.g., 'to shoot straight' vs. 'to get a rabbit'); aims should promote sustained, self‑directed activity rather than static attainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid education as instrument of class exploitation or narrow state ends
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not enough to see to it that education is not actively used as an instrument to make easier the exploitation of one class by another; schools must in fact discount the effects of economic inequalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate systems for whether state or elite interests co‑opt education; require adequate facilities, supplementation of family resources, and curriculum/method changes to secure equal opportunity.
